questions.q: Who were the sons of Judah?
questions.a: Judah’s sons were Perez, Hezron, Carmi, Hur, and Shobal.

questions.q: Who were the sons of Jahath, and what were they called?
questions.a: Jahath’s sons were Ahumai and Lahad, and they were the clans of the Zorathites.

questions.q: Who did Koz father?
questions.a: Koz fathered Anub and Zobebah, and he was the ancestor of the clans of Aharhel.

questions.q: What did Jabez pray to the God of Israel?
questions.a: He prayed that God would bless him, extend his territory, and keep him from harm so that he might not have to endure pain.

questions.q: What was true about Jabez compared to his brothers, and what does his name mean?
questions.a: Jabez was honored more than his brothers, and his name means pain, because his mother had much pain when she bore him.

questions.q: Was Jabez’s prayer answered?
questions.a: Yes, God granted him his prayer.

questions.q: What work did these descendants of Shelah do, and where did they live?
questions.a: They made pottery and lived in Netaim and Gederah, where they worked for the king.

questions.q: Who were the sons of Simeon?
questions.a: Simeon’s sons were Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, and Shaul.

questions.q: What happened to the number of Shimei’s descendants compared to the descendants of Judah?
questions.a: Shimei’s brothers did not have many children, so Shimei’s clan did not grow as large as the descendants of Judah.

questions.q: Name three cities where the descendants of Simeon lived.
questions.a: They lived in Beersheba, Moladah, and Hazar Shual.

questions.q: Name three more places where the descendants of Simeon lived.
questions.a: They also lived in Bilhah, Ezem, and Tolad.

questions.q: Name three more places where the descendants of Simeon lived.
questions.a: They also lived in Bethuel, Hormah, and Ziklag.

questions.q: Until what time did the descendants of Simeon live in these cities?
questions.a: They lived in Beth Marcaboth, Hazar Susim, Beth Biri, and Shaaraim until the time when David became king.

questions.q: How far did the villages of the descendants of Simeon extend?
questions.a: Their villages extended as far as Baal.

questions.q: Who were the leaders named first in this list of clan leaders?
questions.a: The first leaders named were Meshobab, Jamlech, and Joshah, son of Amaziah.

questions.q: Who were seven of the clan leaders named in this verse?
questions.a: Seven of the leaders were Elioenai, Jaakobah, Jeshohaiah, Asaiah, Adiel, Jesimiel, and Benaiah.

questions.q: What happened to the families of these clan leaders?
questions.a: The families of their fathers became very large.

questions.q: Why did some of the sons of Shimei go to Gedor on the east side of the valley?
questions.a: They were seeking pasture for their flocks, and they found abundant and good pasture there.

questions.q: In whose days did these men attack the Meunites?
questions.a: They attacked the Meunites in the days of Hezekiah, king of Judah, and then lived there because there was pasture for their flocks.

questions.q: How many men from Simeon went to Mount Seir, and who were their leaders?
questions.a: 500 men from Simeon went to Mount Seir, and their leaders were Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah, and Uzziel, the sons of Ishi.

questions.q: What did these men do to the remaining Amalekites?
questions.a: They struck down the Amalekites who had escaped, and they have lived there to this day.

commentary.text: —In this chapter we have a further account of Judah, the most numerous and most famous of all the tribes; also an account of Simeon. The most remarkable person in this chapter is Jabez. We are not told upon what account Jabez was more honourable than his brethren; but we find that he was a praying man. The way to be truly great, is to seek to do God's will, and to pray earnestly. Here is the prayer he made. Jabez prayed to the living and true God, who alone can hear and answer prayer; and, in prayer he regarded him as a God in covenant with his people. He does not express his promise, but leaves it to be understood; he was afraid to promise in his own strength, and resolved to devote himself entirely to God. Lord, if thou wilt bless me and keep me, do what thou wilt with me; I will be at thy command and disposal for ever. As the text reads it, this was the language of a most ardent and affectionate desire, Oh that thou wouldest bless me! Four things Jabez prayed for. 1. That God would bless him indeed. Spiritual blessings are the best blessings: God's blessings are real things, and produce real effects. 2. That He would enlarge his coast. That God would enlarge our hearts, and so enlarge our portion in himself, and in the heavenly Canaan, ought to be our desire and prayer. 3. That God's hand might be with him. God's hand with us, to lead us, protect us, strengthen us, and to work all our works in us and for us, is a hand all-sufficient for us. 4. That he would keep him from evil, the evil of sin, the evil of trouble, all the evil designs of his enemies, that they might not hurt, nor make him a Jabez indeed, a man of sorrow. God granted that which he requested. God is ever ready to hear prayer: his ear is not now heavy.
